title: Activation Traffic Playbook and Metrics Heuristic
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook captures a pragmatic traffic-phasing plan for feature activations (hosted API + Dedicated), the lightweight KPI heuristic we use to decide whether to continue ramping, and the immediate contingency actions owners should execute when signals breach thresholds. It is intentionally operational and terse — meant to be run in the activation control room.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: product-ops, release engineers, SRE on-call, solutions engineering (customer-facing rollouts).
- Scope: soft launches, paid-customer canaries, capacity burst plans, and rollback/run-forward decisions through 0% -> 100% traffic.

Quick TL;DR (one line):
Ramp slowly, watch five signals (quality, latency, errors, capacity, cost) with hard thresholds, and move to fallback models or traffic-reduction steps if any two adjacent thresholds trigger within a 30-minute window.

Phased traffic lanes (recommended):
1) Internal beta (0% external) — smoke left for infra and key stakeholders; duration 24–48h.
2) Pilot customers (0.5–2%) — invited customers, observe quality and costs; duration 48–96h.
3) Soft public (1–5%) — low-risk market probes, monitor adoption and sign-ups; duration adaptive.
4) Ramp to medium (5–25%) — validate scaling and retention signals.
5) Open rollout (25–100%) — monitor SLOs, cost exposure; step increases by doubling or fixed increments depending on capacity.

Primary signals and heuristic thresholds (operational):
- Model quality (eval-set pass rate / manual sampling): baseline = 95% pass on golden prompt set. Warning at 92%, critical at 88%. If critical -> stop ramp, trigger quality rollback to previous model variant.
- Latency (p95): baseline <= 450ms for hosted api. Warning >= 600ms, critical >= 900ms. If critical -> shift traffic to lower-latency variant or region.
- Error rate (5xx + client-timeouts): baseline < 0.5%. Warning >= 1.0%, critical >= 2.0%. If critical -> reduce traffic to previous capacity tier and open SRE investigation.
- Capacity / queue length (avg queue > target): warning when queue > 20% of burst buffer, critical when > 50%. If critical -> autoscale burst or throttle non-essential routes.
- Cost per activation (USD per 1k activations): watch for >30% spike vs projection. If cost runaway -> enable batching suggestions, disable non-critical caching misses, and consider quantized variant.

Operational rule-of-thumb (heuristic):
- Continue ramp if at most one signal is at warning and none critical for 60 minutes.
- Pause/investigate if two signals reach warning within 30 minutes.
- Immediate rollback or traffic reduction if any critical signal persists for >15 minutes AND a second signal moves to warning/critical.

Owner matrix (immediate contacts during activation):
- Activation lead / decisions: Maya Chen (product-ops) — final go/no-go on incremental ramp steps.
- SRE escalation: Owen Patel — capacity, autoscaling, infra rollback.
- Quality & evals: Lena Martinez — manual sampling, eval-run orchestration.
- Customer comms / SE: Samir Desai — customer notifications, MRs for customer-specific fallbacks.
- Console/metrics: Jesse Rivera — dashboard changes, alert fingerprints.

Pre-launch checklist (minimum pass to start pilot):
- [ ] Canary model pinned and tested with golden prompts (Lena).
- [ ] Load test 1.5x expected pilot qps (Owen).
- [ ] Cost projection and budget flag set for experiment (product-ops finance tag).
- [ ] Runbook stub written and shared in Slack channel #prod-activation (Maya).
- [ ] Support rotation scheduled for first 72 hours (Samir).
- [ ] API keys and routing rules validated for canary cohort (DevEx).

Realtime monitoring dashboard (must-haves):
- One screen: 1) p95 latency, 2) error rate, 3) qps and queue length, 4) model-eval pass rate (rolling 100 samples), 5) cost burn rate vs projection.
- Alerting: PagerDuty for critical thresholds; Slack digest for warnings every 15 minutes.

Short playbook for common contingencies:
- High latency (p95 >= critical): 1) Temporarily route canary -> nearest-region fallback (Owen, 5m). 2) If latency persists, reduce concurrency per-instance and increase batch size heuristics (SRE, 15m). 3) If fixes fail, rollback to previous compiled variant (Maya, 30m).
- Model-quality regression: 1) Immediately stop ramp and open a triage (Lena, 0–10m). 2) Run a differential eval on the latest commits and golden prompt set (Lena). 3) If regression confirmed, rollback model variant and create hotfix PR to model onboarding repo (github link in artifacts).
- Error spike (>= critical rate): 1) Check infra logs for OOMs/GCs (Owen, 0–10m). 2) If infra healthy, isolate by traffic-tagging a subset of requests to identify a failing prompt pattern (Lena + DevEx, 15–30m). 3) Re-route or mask problematic inputs via prefiltering if needed.

Communication protocol (what to say and when):
- At pilot start: 1-line summary to #prod-ops + stakeholders (traffic %, expected duration, known risks).
- On first warning: quick digest (what tripped, who owns triage, expected next update window).
- On critical: all-hands channel + PD escalation, conference bridge (owner list above). Postmortem to be scheduled within 72 hours.

Data capture for postmortem (minimum):
- Exact timestamps of threshold crossings, dashboards snapshots, representative request ids, model hash + commit, autoscaler events, and cost snapshots.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- [ ] Formalize the golden prompt set for Dedicated customers — currently ad-hoc. (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Add cost burn alarm to billing pipeline (owner: Finance eng contact).
- [ ] Evaluate automated canary rollback policy in the router (PR exists but not tested).
- [ ] Create synthetic workload that mimics 95th percentile token lengths for key customers (owner: SRE).

Appendix: quick ramp plan example (numbers for a medium-sized feature):
- Pilot: 2% traffic for 72h -> success metrics: p95 latency stable, error < 1%, eval pass >= 93% -> proceed.
- Soft: 5% for 48h -> success metrics: retention delta + conversion measured, cost delta within 20% projection -> proceed.
- Medium: 20% for 48h -> runway to 50% if no warnings; else pause and root cause.

Session notes (recent trial 2025-09 pilot):
- Observed: p95 drifted from 420ms to 760ms after 12h due to cache churn on long-tail prompts. Fix: increased KV cache warmup + longer persistence window reduced p95 to 480ms. Cost up 12% but acceptable.
- Learnings: key long-tail customers drove disproportionate queue spikes; next time isolate them into a separate tier during pilot.

End of doc — pragmatic, action-first. Use this as the runbook seed and iterate after each activation postmortem.

Notes to self: keep this doc short; link to larger activation decisioning system in Confluence for archival postmortems and signal definitions.
